lines.text: Twenty twenty-eight.
Agents draw, listen, speak, and train their own models.
Nobody remembers when they couldn't.
But in twenty twenty-six, your smartest worker is locked in a room.
It writes the code for an image model, and never sees the picture.
It reads every transcript, and never hears a voice.
And when it needs a GPU, it stops. And waits. For you.
Sign up. Pick a GPU. Copy a key. Babysit a server.
Forget it running on Friday, and pay for it on Monday.
So we opened the door.
Paste one line, and your agent rents its own GPU, from any provider, in minutes, under your budget.
Any model. Images. Voices. Transcription. Embeddings.
On an OpenAI-compatible endpoint that every tool you have can call.
Its own code, too: it fine-tunes on your data and hands you a model that is yours.
Open models, under your rules. The data stays on the machine; the agent sees the results.
And when the work stops, the GPU stops.
A watchdog on the machine shuts it down, even if the chat is closed, even if you're asleep.
Someday, this will look obvious.
Today, it's one line.
GPU for Agents. Give your agent a GPU.
